runs.text: 12 major fires in churches or meeting halls
Destroyed First Congregational, First Methodist, and First Presbyterian Churches
East Avenue Methodist church (Dec. 17, the first of the series of church fires), $10,000.
First Presbyterian church (moving picture booth fire), $50.
Knights of Pythias temple (first fire in basement, small loss), $150.
Knights of Pythias temple (second fire, heavy loss), $10,000.
Chase block fire (Knights of Columbus quarters), $100,000.

elements.source: SLIDE 013 Photo - Seven of Kalamazoo Forty Churches postcard 1 of 1 (also SLIDE 100).png

runs.text: He wrote, "There are in this village today six Protestant churches and a Catholic church. There is a Baptist church with one hundred seventy-six members; a Methodist with eighty members; St. Luke's with fifty members; a Dutch Reformed with sixty members; a Presbyterian with one hundred eighty, and the Congregational with one hundred sixty.

There are four common schools, one and sometimes two private schools, a Female Seminary, and a Baptist College and Theological Seminary, each in the early stages of their growth. How changed will be the conditions of this place (now numbering between three and four thousand inhabitants) and of this church when this shall be brought forth for the perusal of some distant generation. May He then look down from the heights of Heaven and see Freedom and Christianity over-spreading the earth."
After the fire in 1925, the church’s time capsule was opened, containing a letter written by Rev. A. S. Kedzie.
The library and the Methodist Church
